subject: Finalize DPA language for Order Form (SCCs + transfer addendum)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@novapraxis.com>, Markus Vogel <m.vogel@novapraxis.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer, laura_bennett
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Finalize DPA language for Order Form (SCCs + transfer addendum)

Hi Elena / Markus —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Attached is our working redline to the Order Form DPA (Novapraxis_OrderForm_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm whether you want to incorporate the SCCs as an annex to the DPA (our default suggestion) or reference the EU Commission decision directly in the Order Form and keep a short DPA.
- We proposed a narrow transfer addendum (Section 6) to capture non-EU subprocessors and cross-border routing exceptions — please flag any operational constraints.
- On roles: we suggested a controller/processor mapping table (pg. 3) and a simple delegation clause for subprocessors that requires prior notice for high-risk subprocessors.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: your legal review of the redline with comments
- Thu 6/4: joint review call to resolve open items
- Fri 6/5: final sign-off and DocuSign link circulated if agreed

If you prefer, we can also provide a brief memo that explains which SCCs clause variants map to each operational scenario — happy to do that after your initial review.

Attachments: Novapraxis_OrderForm_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (redline), Redwood_SCCs_Annex_draft.pdf (informational)

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Head of Legal Operations (Contracting)
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0193

--

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@novapraxis.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Vogel <m.vogel@novapraxis.com>, karthik_iyer, laura_bennett
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finalize DPA language for Order Form (SCCs + transfer addendum)

Alex —

Thanks, received. We reviewed the redline quickly and have three immediate flags:

1) Subprocessor notice: we need a shorter notice window for onboarding (proposing 10 business days instead of 30) — our procurement team requires faster confirmation cycles.
2) Encryption/Key management: can you confirm which KMS integrations Redwood supports for customer-managed keys? We need this detail before agreeing to the proposed language in Section 5.
3) Liability carveouts: our counsel is asking to cap processor liability for indirect damages in the DPA — can you advise whether that is a redline we should expect pushback on?

I’m copying Markus (ops) to confirm if any of the transfer addendum routing exceptions will break their EU data residency plan.

We will attempt to turn around marked-up redline by EOD Wed 6/3. If possible, please loop in your privacy counsel prior to the Thu 6/4 call so we can avoid a long legal-only discussion.

Best,
Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Procurement | NovaPraxis
elena.soto@novapraxis.com

Subject: Re: Finalize DPA language for Order Form (SCCs + transfer addendum)

Elena —

Thanks for the early read and flags. Quick responses inline: 

- Subprocessor notice: we can accept 10 business days for non-critical subprocessors. For high-risk subprocessors (model hosting, telemetry, or customer KMS hosting) we request 30 days + right to pause onboarding. If this is acceptable, we will add a short definitional table to avoid ambiguity.

- KMS / CMK: Redwood supports AWS KMS customer-managed keys and a bring-your-own-key flow for GCP (Cloud KMS) in our Private deployment. I’ll add an explicit implementation note to the DPA (new Section 5.2) and a cross-reference to the security whitepaper.

- Liability carveouts: cap on indirect damages — we are generally constrained by our commercial policy for MSA-level liability. For the DPA we can propose a mutual limitation that preserves statutory indemntities for data breaches. If you need specific cap numbers, provide your target and we’ll run with commercial/sales to confirm.

Operational note on SCCs: we recommend embedding the latest EU Commission SCCs template as an annex rather than writing bespoke clauses inline. That keeps the main DPA short and reduces redline surface. I attached a short draft annex (Redwood_SCCs_Annex_draft.pdf) to help the call.

Proposed: Thu 6/4 10:00 AM CET (1:00 AM PT — sorry for the time) — if that doesn’t work for your team, offer two slots.

Forwarding our redline to external counsel for a quick sanity check prior to the joint call.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Hanna Schultz <hanna.schultz@graystone-legal.com>
To: karthik_iyer, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@novapraxis.com>, Markus Vogel <m.vogel@novapraxis.com>, laura_bennett
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Finalize DPA language for Order Form (SCCs + transfer addendum) — counsel notes

Alex / Karthik —

Quick note from external counsel (Graystone): I reviewed your redline + the proposed annex. Short summary before the call: 

1) SCCs: embedding the Commission SCCs as an annex is the cleanest path. Add a short mechanism for updating to future SCC versions by mutual written agreement. Avoid automatic amendment language.

2) Transfer addendum: limit routing exceptions to named non-EU subprocessors and require documented justification per transfer. That will preserve NovaPraxis’s audit posture.

3) Subprocessor notice: 10 business days is reasonable if the onboarding checklist includes security attestations; keep 30 days for anything that involves MI/aggregate telemetry or model training.

4) DocuSign: I prepared a sign-ready version pending your final choices on liability caps. Link: https://www.docusign.com/signed/DP-2026-1147-preview (attachment: DP-2026-1147_Final_for_Signature.pdf)

I’ll join the Thu 6/4 10:00 CET call to walk through open items. If you want me to pre-clear specific language around key revocation and CMK controls, flag those lines and I’ll send a short memo.

Regards,
Hanna Schultz
Partner, Graystone Legal
hanna.schultz@graystone-legal.com
